thumbnails.prompt_en: Photorealistic high-saturation HDR wide shot on the open South China Sea near Scarborough Shoal in bright late-afternoon sun, just before golden hour. In the foreground, filling the left half of the frame, a small weathered gray 1980s Pohang-class corvette flying a small Philippine flag cuts through the waves on patrol, rust streaks and scratched, pitted hull plates in sharp detail, touched by warm glowing orange sunlight, a few Filipino sailors in blue working uniforms on deck looking back over the stern. Behind it, on the right side of the frame and closing in, two much larger modern gray Chinese navy warships with tall angular superstructures follow in its wake, cold and close, their steel catching bright electric blue reflections from the sea. Pale reef water shows in the distance. Tense but natural documentary realism, no weapons firing, no explosions, no oversized flags, no exaggerated faces, the size difference alone tells the story. thumbnails.prompt_en: Photorealistic high-saturation HDR cinematic wide shot at a huge Korean shipyard in Ulsan in bright late-afternoon daylight. The Korean side fills about two-thirds of the frame on the right and in the foreground: a brand-new gray guided-missile frigate built for the Philippine Navy stands finished in a dry dock beneath a giant goliath gantry crane, shot from a heroic slightly low angle, its steel lit by warm golden backlight with a glowing rim light and lens flare. In the foreground, three or four cheerful Korean shipyard workers in blue work uniforms and white hard hats, shown from the waist up, smile and bump fists as they walk past the finished ship, their proud, confident expressions clearly readable. A huge Korean flag Taegukgi waves proudly in sunlight in the upper right sky, about a quarter of the frame height, not covering the people or the ship. On the left edge, one-third of the frame or less behind a soft diagonal boundary, a rusty old 1960s gray ex-US Coast Guard cutter sits stuck on a coral reef in shallow tropical water, in full color but desaturated and dusty, with faded paint and rust streaks, a small plain Philippine flag on its mast, no people. The dock, crane and shipyard make the location obvious at a glance. Triumphant, victorious, epic cinematic mood, no mockery.
